sql-elastic-pool-single-database.title: A pool of one database rarely saves money
sql-elastic-pool-single-database.body: This estimate has one database in the elastic pool. Microsoft states that the savings from a pool grow with the number of databases that share it, so a single database is usually cheaper as a standalone database.

citation.quote: The more databases you can add to a pool, the greater your savings.

sql-elastic-pool-reserve.title: A steady pool can use reserved capacity
sql-elastic-pool-reserve.body: This pool runs all month on pay-as-you-go and you expect steady use. Microsoft recommends reserving compute capacity for one or three years once the compute size is known; a reservation discounts pool vCores (not eDTU pools).

citation.quote: use that information to reserve the capacity for one or three years.

sql-elastic-pool-hybrid-benefit.title: Azure Hybrid Benefit can remove the SQL license charge
sql-elastic-pool-hybrid-benefit.body: This vCore pool pays the SQL Server license as part of the price. If the customer owns SQL Server licenses with Software Assurance, Azure Hybrid Benefit discounts that license charge.

citation.source: Plan and manage costs for Azure SQL Database
citation.quote: In the provisioned compute tier of the vCore-based purchasing model, you can get a discount on the allocation of SQL Server licenses to SQL Server Database Engine.

sql-elastic-pool-edtu-vcore.title: eDTU pools cannot use reserved capacity
sql-elastic-pool-edtu-vcore.body: This estimate uses an eDTU pool (Basic, Standard or Premium). Microsoft states that reserved instance pricing is only available in the vCore purchasing model, so a pool that runs steadily may cost less as a vCore pool with a 1- or 3-year reservation.

citation.source: vCore purchasing model - Azure SQL Database
citation.quote: Reserved instance pricing is only available for vCore purchasing model.
